finding.shortLabel: Record coverage: a continuous 1641-1663 civic/land/court/probate footprint
finding.statement: John Gurney's surviving documentary footprint is broad within four record classes — colony court and account records, town land books (Weymouth, Braintree, Billerica, Mendon), a registry deed, a court deposition, and probate (as witness/appraiser and as decedent) — and runs continuously from his earliest secure record (the 2 June 1641 Weymouth gunpowder-fine remission) to his 16 March 1663 estate inventory.

sources.locator: Great Migration Directory, 2nd ed. (2025), p. 158 (John Gurney entry)

finding.statement: Anderson's Great Migration Directory (2nd ed., 2025), p. 158, summarizes John Gurney's documented New England presence — arrival 1636, settlements Boston and Braintree — records his English origin as 'Unknown,' and rests the entry on six cited records (Winthrop's Journal 2:422; Massachusetts Bay Records 1:331; NEHGR 62:94; Suffolk Probate Case #338; History of Weymouth 3:251; The American Genealogist 10:70-73); it omits the Weymouth residential phase the manuscript town-land records attest.
